extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (agents/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining whether a claim limitation invoking 35 U.S.C. 112(f) (or pre‑AIA 112 sixth paragraph) is definite and supported by corresponding structure/material/acts in the specification, and special guidance for computer‑implemented means‑plus‑function limitations (algorithm disclosure, general‑purpose computer limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invocation of 35 U.S.C. 112(f) does not exempt other 112 requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The invocation of 35 U.S.C. 112(f) does not exempt an applicant from compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112(a) and 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (or pre‑AIA first and second paragraphs). Means‑plus‑function language can be used in the claims, but the claims must still accurately define the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cases: Donaldson; In re Knowlton. Examiners must ensure written description and definiteness requirements are met even when 112(f) is invoked; a means‑plus‑function limitation cannot avoid those statutory duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification must disclose sufficient corresponding structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must disclose structure (or material or acts) corresponding to the recited means‑ (or step‑) plus‑function; the inquiry is whether one skilled in the art would understand the specification itself to disclose a structure, not merely whether that person could implement the structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite: Atmel; Biomedino. It is insufficient for the patentee to merely state or argue that persons of ordinary skill would know what structures to use. Drawings may supply the disclosure in proper circumstances (Vas‑Cath). If one skilled in the art cannot identify structure from the specification, a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly link/associate disclosed structure to the claimed function
rubrics_metrics.description: The structure disclosed in the written description is corresponding structure only if the specification or prosecution history clearly links or associates that structure to the function recited in the means‑plus‑function limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite: B. Braun; Telcordia. The link is the quid pro quo for employing 112(f). If one skilled in the art cannot identify what structure/material/acts perform the claimed function, a 112(b) rejection is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer‑implemented 112(f) limitations require disclosure of an algorithm
rubrics_metrics.description: For a computer‑implemented 35 U.S.C. 112(f) claim limitation, the specification must disclose an algorithm for performing the claimed specific computer function, or else the claim is indefinite under 35 U.S.C. 112(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite: NetMoneyIN; In re Aoyama; WMS Gaming. The disclosed structure for a computer‑implemented function is the special‑purpose computer programmed to perform the disclosed algorithm, not merely a general‑purpose computer alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: General‑purpose computer alone is insufficient except in rare coextensive cases
rubrics_metrics.description: A microprocessor or general purpose computer serves as structure only where the claimed function is coextensive with the microprocessor itself; most computer‑implemented functions require disclosure of an algorithm (special programming).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite: EON Corp.; In re Katz; Ergo Licensing. Examples of functions that may be coextensive: 'receiving', 'storing', 'processing' data. All other computer‑implemented functions require an algorithm disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithm may be expressed in any understandable form
rubrics_metrics.description: An algorithm may be expressed as a mathematical formula, in prose, in a flow chart, or in any other manner that provides sufficient structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite: Finisar; Microsoft Computer Dictionary. Source code listing is not required; the algorithm must be a finite sequence of steps that sufficiently describe how to perform the claimed function so a person of ordinary skill can implement it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of algorithm judged by one skilled in the art
rubrics_metrics.description: If the specification explicitly discloses an algorithm, the sufficiency of that disclosure is determined in light of the level of ordinary skill in the art; the examiner should determine whether one skilled in the art would know how to program the computer to perform the necessary steps (enablement and written description).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite: Aristocrat; AllVoice; Intel. If the algorithm disclosure is adequate, it can convert a general purpose microprocessor into a special purpose computer for claim support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithm must cover all claimed functions of a multi‑function limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: When a means‑plus‑function limitation performs multiple identifiable functions, the specification must disclose adequate corresponding structure/algorithm for all of the claimed functions; disclosure for only some functions is treated as if no algorithm were disclosed for the others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite: Williamson; Noah. Example: 'distributed learning control module' required structure for 'receiving', 'relaying', and 'coordinating' — failure to disclose algorithm for 'coordinating' rendered the limitation indefinite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere high‑level outcome descriptions or general 'software' recitations are insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions that merely state the outcome of a function, or mere references to a general purpose computer, 'software', 'logic', or an undefined component (black box) do not adequately disclose corresponding structure for 112(f) support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite: Aristocrat; Blackboard; Finisar; NetMoneyIN. Anti‑pattern: labeling a component 'access control manager' without explaining how it performs the function. Such abstractions support a 112(b) rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: No reliance on incorporated‑by‑reference or prior art for corresponding structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The corresponding structure/material/acts cannot include any structure disclosed only in material incorporated by reference or in a prior art reference; the specification itself must disclose the structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite: Pressure Prods.; Atmel; Default Proof. Office personnel must review the specification without reliance on incorporated documents; merely mentioning prior art references does not give patentable claim to structures in those references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner procedure: determine function then review written description for corresponding structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the examiner determines that a claim limitation is a means‑plus‑function limitation invoking 112(f), the examiner should determine the claimed function and then review the written description of the specification (including drawings) to determine whether corresponding structure/material/acts that perform the claimed function are disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings, figures, tables, sequence listings may provide the disclosure (Vas‑Cath). If the examiner cannot identify corresponding structure, make a 112(b) rejection and consider a requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three primary situations warranting 112(b) rejection when 112(f) is invoked
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (or pre‑AIA 112 second paragraph) may be appropriate when: (1) it is unclear whether a limitation invokes 112(f); (2) 112(f) is invoked and there is no or insufficient disclosure of structure/material/acts; and/or (3) 112(f) is invoked and the supporting disclosure fails to clearly link or associate disclosed structure/material/acts to the claimed function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should document which of the three situations applies. If invocation is ambiguous, consider claim language, specification, and how a skilled artisan would understand the claim in light of the disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguous claim language requires holistic assessment and opportunity to amend
rubrics_metrics.description: If the 3‑prong analysis for determining whether 112(f) applies is inconclusive because of ambiguous words in the claim, the examiner, after considering the claims, specification, and skilled artisan understanding, should determine whether the claim recites sufficiently definite structure; applicants have opportunity to present arguments or amend claims to clarify applicability of 112(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant disagrees, they may amend or argue during prosecution to clarify whether 112(f) applies; examiners should make a reasoned determination based on the whole record.

rubrics_metrics.name: If examiner cannot identify corresponding structure, require information or reject
rubrics_metrics.description: When the examiner cannot identify the corresponding structure/material/acts, a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) should be made. The examiner may issue a requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105 to require identification of the corresponding structure; failure to timely reply may result in abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §704.11(a) Example R and §704.12 — requirement for information must be complete and replied to within set time (including extensions). If applicant lacks information or does not identify structure, make the 112(b) rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means‑plus‑function limitation limits claim to disclosed structure and equivalents (no importing nonrecited functions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the written description sets forth corresponding structure/material/acts in compliance with 112(b), the claim limitation must be construed to cover that disclosed structure/material/acts and equivalents. Functional limitations not recited in the claim, or structural limitations in the specification unnecessary to perform the claimed function, cannot be imported into the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite: Welker; Wenger. Examiner and courts construe the claim to the disclosed corresponding structure and its equivalents; applicants cannot expand claim scope by importing extra elements from the spec.

rubrics_metrics.name: When 112(b) indefiniteness for lack of corresponding structure exists, written description and enablement concerns follow
rubrics_metrics.description: A means‑plus‑function limitation found indefinite under 112(b) for failure to disclose sufficient corresponding structure will also lack adequate written description under 112(a) and may not be enabled to support the full scope of the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should consider whether disclosure contains sufficient information to enable one skilled in the art to make and use the full scope of the claimed invention (see MPEP §§2161.01, 2163.03, 2164.08). Cite: Ariad (genus/species functional claiming concerns).

rubrics_metrics.name: If structure described only in broad generic terms with details incorporated by reference, applicant may be required to amend spec
rubrics_metrics.description: If corresponding structure/material/acts are described in broad generic terms and the specific details are incorporated by reference, the Office must review the specification without relying on the incorporated document; if one skilled in the art would not be able to identify the structure from the spec, the applicant will be required to amend the specification to include the relevant portions of the referenced document (37 CFR 1.57(d)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not require insertion of entire referenced document—applicant should include only the relevant portions that correspond to the means‑plus‑function limitation. Cite: Default Proof; 37 CFR 1.57(d)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special guidance on mode of implementation (hardware vs software) for 112(f) limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: By choosing to use a means‑plus‑function limitation and invoke 112(f), the applicant limits that claim limitation to the disclosed structure (implementation by hardware or combination of hardware and software) and equivalents; the examiner should not construe the limitation as covering pure software implementation when the disclosure indicates hardware or hardware/software combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no corresponding structure is disclosed (i.e., only software per se without an algorithm and corresponding programmed computer), the limitation should be deemed indefinite and rejected under 112(b). However, a claim including such an indefinite limitation is not necessarily directed as a whole to software per se unless it lacks other structural limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case examples illustrating insufficiency (symbol generator; compliance mechanism; access control)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the specification describes only general terms (e.g., symbols generated based on latitude/longitude) without an operative algorithm, or includes source code that only returns error messages, courts have found the means‑plus‑function limitations indefinite for lack of an algorithm or structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Advanced Ground Information Systems v. Life360 (symbol generator indefinite for no algorithm); Media Rights v. Capital One (copyright compliance mechanism lacked algorithms for diverting/managing/monitoring functions); Blackboard, Inc. (access control manager described outcome but not structure). These examples guide examiners on borderline adequacy issues.
